title: Unbelief the Soul Dismays
description: Unbelief the Soul Dismays in Tonic Solfa to VIENNA, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book III, hymn 39, “Great effects by weak means”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to VIENNA; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Un-be-lief the soul dis-mays, What ob-jec-tions will it raise! But true faith se-cure-ly leans On the pro-mise, in the means.

lines: Unbelief the soul dismays,
What objections will it raise!
But true faith securely leans
On the promise, in the means.
If to faith it once be known,
God has said, "It shall be done,
And in this appointed way;"
Faith has then no more to say.
Moses' rod, by faith upreared,
Through the sea a path prepared;
Jericho's devoted wall,
At the trumpet's sound must fall.
With a pitcher and a lamp,
Gideon overthrew a camp
And a stone, well aimed by faith,
Proved the armed Philistine's death.
Thus the Lord is pleased to try
Those who on his help rely;
By the means he makes it known,
That the pow'r is all his own.
Yet the means are not in vain,
If the end we would attain;
Though the breath of prayer be weak,
None shall find, but they who seek.
God alone the heart can reach;
Yet the ministers must preach;
'Tis their part the seed to sow,
And 'tis his to make it grow.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to VIENNA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
